text:
anna: Heads-up — saw steady memory growth on two nightly GPU nodes serving long-context workloads. rsz (RSS) +1.1GB over ~30m under steady QPS. attaching flamegraph in thread.
perf-bot: PERF ALERT: memory_growth >500MB in 15m on r-infer-03 (job=longctx-stream)
mike: ugh. did anything touch cache key derivation in the last week? I recall a small refactor around session keys.
jess: yes — PR #4521 added request.trace_id to the cache key to help trace cold-start misses. it improved visibility but i didn’t think about reuse semantics.
sam: that explains it: trace_id is unique per request -> keys stop colliding -> zero prefix reuse -> hotset explodes -> fragmentation + paging. observed a ton of tiny entries in kv pages.
anna: profiling: kv_cache miss rate jumped from ~12% to ~67% after that deploy. tail latency +120ms. flamegraph points to kv_store::insert_path allocating heavily and frequent page splits.
mike: can we revert quickly? or better: patch key gen to strip ephemeral fields (trace_id/req_id) for prefix keys. we still need trace_id for logs, but not cache identity.
jess: proposed quick fix: separate "observability key" and "cache key". cache key = sha(prefix_tokens || tenant_id || session_salt) — explicitly exclude trace_id. pseudo:
```
// in runtime/cache_key.rs
let mut h = Sha256::new();
h.update(prefix_bytes);
h.update(tenant_id.as_bytes());
h.update(session_salt.as_bytes());
let cache_key = h.finalize();
```
also add an opt-in sticky_session_id for workloads that want affinity.
sam: two follow-ups: 1) sticky_session mapping across shards — include session_id in consistent-hash to pick same worker, or maintain a small mapping store. 2) mapping memory: need TTL + LRU, otherwise we trade one leak for another.
anna: also noticed an interaction with batching heuristics: batcher coalesced long-prefix requests with short ones; kernel selection then picked a large-seq kernel which triggered more KV writes per token and increased page churn.
mike: so batching change + trace_id change amplified the regression. mitigation: add batcher rule to avoid grouping requests when max_prefix - min_prefix > 128 tokens. cheap fix in heuristic.
jess: agreed. action plan:
- strip ephemeral IDs from cache keys (hotfix)
- add sticky_session_id support with TTLed mapping
- batcher threshold change to avoid mismatched prefix coalescing
- expose metrics: kv_prefix_key_miss, kv_fragmentation_pages, kv_page_evictions, session_affinity_size, sticky_mapping_evictions
- canary 10% then 2h observation before rollout
perf-bot: ACTIONS created: INV-1723 strip-ephemeral-ids-from-key, INV-1724 batcher-prefix-length-gap, INV-1725 sticky-session-ttl
sam: i'll implement INV-1723 + tests. test harness: replay same prefix with different trace_ids; assert miss rate stays low and resident set stable across 30m synthetic run.
mike: for INV-1724 i'll open a small PR to enqueue split rule and add unit tests for the heuristic. also add a regression test in perf suite to simulate batching with mixed prefix lengths.
anna: for INV-1725 we need an ops knob: default sticky_ttl=30m and mapping max_entries=100k. ops can tune per deployment. we should also expose mapping size in Console.
jess: docs: update runtime/README cache-key semantics + add note in release notes for the hotfix. also update eval harness to include a "cache-key-sanity" test that injects random trace_ids.
perf-bot: canary plan scheduled: 10% traffic -> 2h retention -> auto rollback on kv_page_evictions > baseline*1.2 or kv_prefix_miss > baseline*1.5
sam: quick caveat: stripping trace_id reduces our ability to tie a cold miss to a specific request in logs. suggest generating a separate observability token that uses trace_id but not used for caching.
mike: yep keep observability token separate. logs and traces unaffected.
anna: timeline? we need hotfix asap.
mike: target: patch tonight, canary tomorrow morning (UTC), full rollout if green within 24h.
jess: i'll shepherd release + update changelog.
sam: starting work now, will post draft PR and perf-run results in this thread. :rocket:
anna: thanks — keep updates compact here. if we see any other regressions after patch, escalate to incidents channel.
mike: ack. :thumbsup:
